attribution.note: Marcus wrote these words in his own Substack post. The nearby Wierda estimate is quoted separately and is not part of this sentence.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition matches the sentence. 'Possible' qualifies only the productivity description. The claim that coding burns the most cash is stated firmly in the present tense, so it is an observation.

contract.note: Reading 'burning the most cash' as the largest net cash outflow by use case, in the latest quarter completed before the post, is an ordinary plain reading. How shared costs are allocated is ambiguous, but no available evidence turns on that choice.

evidence.note: The Anthropic S-1 was available before the cutoff. It reports one operating segment and no split between coding and other uses, so it cannot rank cash burn by application.
This report shows how much Claude was used for coding in February 2026. It measures usage, not cash outflows, so it cannot show which use case burned the most cash.

reviews.rationale: Neither item in the packet gives net cash burn by AI use case for January–March 2026. The filing reports only consolidated figures, and the usage report has no financial data. Sources that might have helped could not be read. Nothing in the packet establishes or refutes that coding burned the most cash.
